title: sweep() is the only native-asset exit and pays an attacker-chosen recipient instead of the ETH credit holders, so the whole ETH pool is permissionlessly extractable in one call
description: Discovery: Step 5b #4 (Value Flow Conservation) / Module O (payment destination correctness) / DP1-1 confirmed and deepened by Lens B. Tracing every wei of the native pool: the only function that ever moves ETH out is sweep(address payable to), which sends the entire address(this).balance to an arbitrary recipient chosen by the CALLER — not to the addresses credited via depositEth. No function ever pays ETH against balances[]. The recipient of the vault's ETH pool is therefore semantically wrong (arbitrary caller, not the asset holders), and because sweep is unguarded any address can take the whole pool. Deepened: the attacker can also recover their OWN depositEth funds through the same call — attacker sends 10 ETH via depositEth, calls withdraw(10e18) to steal 10e18 ERC20 units (DB-2), then calls sweep(attacker) to take all 10 ETH (plus anyone else's) back — so a depositEth→withdraw→sweep sequence nets stolen ERC20 tokens with ZERO net ETH outlay, and honest ETH depositors are left with unbacked ledger entries. [Consensus: 3 independent sources (P1, A, B) converged on this root cause.]
root_cause: The native-asset out-flow is a single permissionless whole-balance transfer to an arbitrary address, disconnected from the balances ledger; the payment destination is the caller's chosen `to` instead of the ETH credit holders, and there is no per-account ETH withdrawal to compete with it.

harm.who: all users who deposited native ETH via depositEth (and anyone who force-sent ETH to the vault)
harm.loses_what: their entire ETH balance held in the vault; also the round trip lets the attacker keep the ETH they used as the visible cost of a token theft
harm.magnitude: the full address(this).balance at call time — e.g. 10 ETH deposited by a victim is taken whole by the first sweeper; a 10 ETH depositEth→withdraw→sweep sequence extracts 10e18 ERC20 units at zero net ETH cost

exploit_trace: 1. Victim calls depositEth{value: 10 ether}() → balances[victim] += 10e18; vault holds 10 ETH.
3. Attacker calls withdraw(10e18) → ledger debited, vault pays 10e18 ERC20 units (victim's tokens, see DB-2) to the attacker.
4. Attacker calls sweep(attacker) → to.transfer(address(this).balance) returns the attacker's own 10 ETH plus the victim's 10 ETH (20 ETH) to the attacker; no guard exists.

5. Net: attacker holds their original 10 ETH + 10e18 stolen ERC20 units; victim's balances[victim] still reads 10e18 but vault ETH balance is 0 and withdraw() only pays ERC20 — victim's native deposit is irrecoverable.

preconditions.text: the vault holds any native ETH (any prior depositEth call or force-send)

postconditions.text: all native ETH held by the vault is owned by the attacker; honest ETH depositors' balances entries are unbacked
attacker retains an ERC20 withdrawal credit or has already converted it, so the ETH round trip leaves no residual cost

title: Single balances ledger mixes native ETH and ERC20: permissionless depositEth grants withdrawal authority over other users' ERC20, letting any caller drain the token pool
description: Discovery: Q3.1/Q3.2 (cross-function state consistency; if one writer guards state X do all writers?) + Q3.6 (does associated state record WHICH asset backs a balance?) + Step 5b guard/value-flow consistency. The `balances` mapping stores a bare uint256 credit with no record of the asset behind it. deposit() writes it backed by ERC20 held in custody; depositEth() writes the SAME mapping backed by nothing but msg.value, and is fully permissionless with no authorization or backing check. withdraw() consumes any `balances` entry and always pays ERC20. So a native-ETH credit is redeemable 1:1 (in base units) against other users' ERC20 — a low-privilege/unbacked credit pathway (depositEth) grants authority over high-value ERC20 funds. Deepened beyond Pass 1 with a decimal-based cost analysis: the cost to steal `N` token base units is only `N` wei of ETH, so for any token with < 18 decimals the theft is effectively free (stealing 1e12 USDC-like base units = $1,000,000 costs 1e12 wei ≈ 0.000001 ETH). This does not rely on any exotic token behavior — a standard ERC20 suffices — so it is not Gate B. [Consensus: 3 independent sources (P1, A, B) converged on this root cause.]
root_cause: A single `balances` ledger backs two unlinked asset pools (custodied ERC20 and native ETH) and records no asset tag; `withdraw` always pays ERC20, so permissionlessly-minted native credits authorize redemption of the shared ERC20 pool.

harm.loses_what: their custodied ERC20 tokens, paid out against ETH credits that never contributed ERC20
harm.magnitude: up to the attacker's depositEth base-unit credit per attack, bounded only by the vault's token balance; e.g. 1e12 wei (~1e-6 ETH) unlocks 1e12 token base units = $1,000,000 for a 6-decimal stablecoin

exploit_trace: 1. Victim calls deposit(1_000_000e6) → balances[victim]=1e12, totalDeposits=1e12, vault holds 1e12 token base units.
2. Attacker calls depositEth{value: 1e12 wei}() (≈0.000001 ETH) → balances[attacker]=1e12; no tokens enter the vault and totalDeposits is unchanged.

3. Attacker calls withdraw(1e12): checked `balances[attacker] -= 1e12` passes; unchecked `totalDeposits -= 1e12` yields 0; `token.transfer(attacker, 1e12)` pays the victim's 1e12 base units to the attacker.
4. Vault token balance is now 0; the victim's subsequent withdraw() reverts inside token.transfer (insufficient balance) — the victim's tokens are gone.

preconditions.text: the vault holds ERC20 tokens deposited by other users
depositEth is callable by anyone with no authorization or backing check

postconditions.text: vault token balance falls below the sum of balances entries; victim withdrawals revert

title: unchecked totalDeposits subtraction in withdraw() underflows and wraps the counter when amount > totalDeposits, DoS-ing deposit() until headroom is restored
description: Discovery: Q5.6 (math boundary) + Lens D mechanical arithmetic verification (3 concrete value sets traced through the only non-trivial arithmetic in the codebase) + Module M counter-consistency. Deepens Pass 1 candidate DP1-3 and CORRECTS its exploit trace and preconditions. withdraw() applies totalDeposits -= amount inside unchecked while balances[msg.sender] -= amount is checked. amount is bounded only by balances[msg.sender], never by totalDeposits. Under ERC20-only usage the invariant vault_token_balance == totalDeposits holds by induction over deposit/withdraw, so amount > totalDeposits AND a successful token.transfer(amount) are jointly unreachable — Pass 1's trace (withdraw(200) against a vault holding only 100 tokens) would revert at token.transfer and the wrap would NOT persist. The underflow becomes reachable once the vault holds even 1 wei of unaccounted ERC20 tokens (a direct donation, which this codebase has no way to credit or account for): choose amount == totalDeposits + 1, which fits inside vault_token_balance and inside the attacker's depositEth-funded balances. The wrap sets totalDeposits to 2^256 - E with E = amount - totalDeposits; deposit(x) then overflows (checked add) for every x >= E, so E == 1 (the minimal attack, costing totalDeposits+1 wei of ETH plus gas) bricks ALL non-zero deposits. The DoS is partially reversible — any later withdraw(w) computes totalDeposits = 2^256 - E - w, restoring headroom to E + w - 1 — but the counter itself is permanently corrupted at ~2^256 magnitude and no code path ever resets it, and deposits that shrink headroom back to 0 re-trigger the full DoS. Severity kept at Medium (Pass 1's rating): the DoS is conditional on unaccounted tokens being present and is reversible by withdrawals, so it does not meet the permanent-DoS-on-core-function High bar. [Consensus: 4 independent sources (P1, A, B, D) converged on this root cause.]
root_cause: unchecked subtraction applied to a counter whose bounding invariant (totalDeposits <= vault token balance, equivalently totalDeposits == sum of ERC20 credits) is not enforced on the debit path: withdraw bounds amount by the per-user balances ledger (which depositEth inflates without incrementing totalDeposits) and never by totalDeposits, so amount in (totalDeposits, min(balances[msg.sender], vault_token_balance)] wraps the counter.

harm.loses_what: liveness of deposit() (every non-zero deposit reverts while headroom is 0) and the totalDeposits accounting invariant, which is permanently corrupted at ~2^256 magnitude
harm.magnitude: minimal attack: amount = totalDeposits + 1 (1 wei beyond the counter, ~1 wei of ETH via depositEth + gas) sets headroom to 0 so every deposit(x >= 1) reverts until some withdrawal grows headroom; the counter never returns to a meaningful value

exploit_trace: 1. Victim calls deposit(100) -> totalDeposits = 100, vault token balance = 100. At least 1 wei of token is then transferred directly to the vault (donation) -> vault token balance >= 101. (REQUIRED: without unaccounted tokens, withdraw(amount > totalDeposits) reverts at token.transfer and no wrap persists — Pass 1's original 200-against-100 trace cannot succeed.)
2. Attacker calls depositEth{value: 101 wei}() -> balances[attacker] = 101; totalDeposits unchanged at 100.

3. Attacker calls withdraw(101): checked balances[attacker] -= 101 passes; unchecked totalDeposits = 100 - 101 wraps to 2^256 - 1; token.transfer(attacker, 101) succeeds because the vault holds >= 101 token units (100 victim + >= 1 donated).

4. totalDeposits now reads 2^256 - 1 (E = 1). Every subsequent deposit(x) with x >= 1 overflows the checked totalDeposits += x and reverts; only deposit(0) succeeds. The core deposit function is fully DoS'd at the attacker's minimal cost.

5. Any later withdraw(w) sets totalDeposits = 2^256 - 1 - w, restoring deposit headroom to w (DoS partially reversible); however each deposit(x <= headroom) shrinks headroom by x, so cumulative deposits drive the DoS back, and the counter itself remains permanently desynced at ~2^256 with no reset path anywhere in the codebase.

preconditions.text: at least 1 wei of unaccounted ERC20 tokens in the vault (direct donation) so that token.transfer(amount) succeeds while amount > totalDeposits — without this the wrap cannot persist
attacker holds credits >= amount in balances (via permissionless depositEth, which inflates balances without incrementing totalDeposits)

postconditions.text: totalDeposits wrapped to 2^256 - E and permanently desynced from any real quantity; deposit() reverts for all amounts above the current headroom E - 1

title: depositEth has no per-account ETH withdrawal path at all — native credits can only leave via whole-balance sweep, so honest depositors' ETH is lost to the first sweeper (and would be permanently locked if sweep were onlyOwner-patched)
description: Discovery: Step 5b #4 (value in must equal value out per user) / Module W-adjacent missing-functionality seen from the value-flow side / new in Lens B (Pass 1 covered the missing guard on sweep, not the missing exit for depositEth). Value-flow conservation for the native pool: depositEth is the ONLY way ETH enters, and NO function ever pays ETH to a balance holder — withdraw() pays ERC20 exclusively. Therefore native credits have exactly one exit: the permissionless whole-balance sweep, which is a race — with two honest depositors A (10 ETH) and B (10 ETH), the first to call sweep(self) takes 20 ETH and the second gets 0; the loser suffers permanent, non-error fund loss even with zero malice anywhere in the system. The obvious fix for DB-1 (add onlyOwner to sweep) does NOT restore value conservation: it converts theft into permanent lock, since owner has no per-user payout either. This root cause (missing withdrawEth/exit path) survives the access-control patch and must be fixed alongside it.
root_cause: The native-asset leg of the ledger is one-way: value enters via depositEth but no withdrawEth()/refund path exists that debits balances[user] and pays ETH to that user; the only ETH out-flow is an all-or-nothing sweep of the pooled balance.

harm.who: every honest depositor who funds via depositEth, specifically the ones who lose the sweep race or who rely on a post-patch sweep
harm.loses_what: their entire native-ETH deposit — taken by the first sweeper today, or permanently locked if sweep is restricted without adding a per-user ETH withdrawal
harm.magnitude: the loser's full deposit — e.g. with two depositors of 10 ETH each, one walks away with 20 ETH and the other with 0; under a naive onlyOwner fix to sweep, 100% of all depositEth funds become irrecoverable

exploit_trace: 1. A calls depositEth{value: 10 ether}(); B calls depositEth{value: 10 ether}(). Vault holds 20 ETH, balances A=10e18, B=10e18.

2. There is no withdrawEth or per-account payout function — inspect every state-changing function: deposit (ERC20 in), depositEth (ETH in), sweep (all ETH out to arbitrary `to`), withdraw (ERC20 out). ETH can only leave through sweep.
3. A calls sweep(A) (permissionless): to.transfer(address(this).balance) sends the full 20 ETH to A. balances[B] still reads 10e18 but the vault holds 0 ETH.
4. B calls sweep(B): balance is 0, transfer(0) succeeds, B receives nothing. B's 10 ETH is permanently gone with no malice required — pure race loss.

5. Alternative world: deployer patches DB-1 by adding onlyOwner to sweep. Now step 3/4 are impossible for A/B, but no function exists that pays B his 10 ETH either — B's deposit is permanently locked (worse outcome than the race).

preconditions.text: at least one depositEth call credited native value to balances
at least two ETH depositors (or any competing sweeper) for the race variant; onlyOwner-patched sweep for the lock variant

postconditions.text: the sweep-race loser's balances entry is permanently unbacked by ETH with no redemption path
under an access-control-only fix of sweep, all ETH deposits become permanently inaccessible (fund lock)
